text:
Now in beta: Businesses in ChatGPT.

Claim your business, manage your information, and get insights on how people engage with you.

Eligible businesses can also build a Business Agent to answer customers’ questions and help them explore what you offer.

https://t.co/N2GEZX0mFT https://t.co/lYj2Z48fhQ
description: 48-second beta launch for Businesses in ChatGPT: bright white canvas, big black kinetic type ('Your business,') and floating 3D shopping objects that walk through claiming a listing, managing info and building a Business Agent. A clean reference for type-led product intros that keep the UI simple and the motion playful.
replies_summary: Replies to this post are mostly practical feedback, with some spam and bot tags mixed in. People like FAQ-answering business agents but say the claim flow has to lead to real action, not just a stats page. Others complain about it being US-only and about ChatGPT UI changes in general.

notable_replies.text: The insights only earn their keep if the owner can act in the same place: a claimed listing that can answer "do you have this in stock" beats a dashboard nobody opens.
Cool feature, but if u make me go through the whole setup just to tell me it's US-only at the end, that's a scam. Small biz outside the US just got ghosted again.
Business agents answering FAQs makes sense fr

description: Vercel's 'Introducing the UI SDK' launch film (~1:42): it opens on a stark black title card with the boxed 'UI SDK' wordmark and builds the story with typed copy before getting to the product demos. A good reference for a minimal, brand-consistent developer-tool launch where a four-word post lets the video do all the talking.
replies_summary: Reactions are mixed. Some people are impressed (one says they one-shotted an ecommerce port). Others ask how it differs from just starting from shadcn base components, and another user explains that shared 'behavior primitives' are the difference. Many replies are @bot summon requests.

notable_replies.text:
I have One shotted an ecommerce port. Really inpressed.
Ui SDK Is awesome.
Vue support Is what its makes perfect.
But what's the difference with just taking a shadcn base component (or any other) and build your own component from there? I still don't get the value for this.

Because the same behavior is shared between multiple components, so instead of creating 10 component primitives you create 2 behavior primitives so that agent could create that 10 component primitives itself and then build the actual UI component composing them together.

text:
Got to experience the magic of @uisdk.

Two prompts of fx + Gemini Argon. Pure Web Components. No framework.

The agent reused 14 UI SDK behaviors out of the box 🤯: window resizing, drag, menubar hover-switching,  typeahead, roving toolbar focus, 10-band EQ sliders, scoped hotkeys, ARIA, and WebMCP agent control.

https://t.co/1Ol3xqKWJz (source linked)
Music by @suno.
description: Guillermo Rauch demos a pixel-faithful Winamp clone running in the browser (winamp-ui-sdk.vercel.app), built from two prompts with UI SDK. It shows window resizing, drag, menubar hover-switching, 10-band EQ sliders and hotkeys, set to Suno music. A delightful reference for nostalgic, highly interactive web UI and for showing off micro-interactions in a screen recording.
replies_summary: Most replies are excited, and people single out the 14 reusable behaviors (focus, typeahead, keyboard nav) as the real win. A few push back: design fidelity is lacking, and does accessibility hold up beyond looks? There is also nostalgia for 'UI making me feel emotions again'.

notable_replies.text: Oh am I so absolutely ready for UI to go back to making me feel emotions again
But it doesn't look the same, design detail is of utter importance here, and it's lacking big time.
two prompts to undo twenty years of product management, this is great

text:
Obsidian 1.15.1 is now available!

- Search is revamped with faster results, Relevance sort, and accent-insensitive matching.
- New Android widgets! View notes on your home screen.
- Web Viewer on mobile. Turn it on in Core plugins to open web pages from within Obsidian.

Dozens of performance improvements and fixes across the app:

- On desktop, the workspace now appears right away while Obsidian starts, with start-up progress in the status bar instead of a loading screen.
- Large canvases now open, pan, and zoom much faster.
- Smart lists prevents over-indenting list items.
- New vaults no longer show the ribbon.
- Live Preview: Opening a note no longer shows the Markdown syntax at the cursor (e.g. the ## of a heading on the first line) until you move the cursor or start typing.
- Hold Ctrl/Cmd while picking a vault from the sidebar to replace the current window instead of opening a new one.
- iOS Voice capture now starts a new line when you pause speaking for 2 seconds.
- Android: Obsidian starts faster in vaults with large hidden folders, such as .git.
description: Short (~11s) release clip for Obsidian 1.15.1 showing the revamped search: a pill-shaped search field with cursor, relevance sorting and instant results in the native macOS window. A tight reference for single-feature UI demo clips attached to a changelog-style post.
replies_summary: Users love the faster startup, the widgets and accent-insensitive search (multilingual users especially). Some ask for an iOS native app and multi-window vaults, and one argues that search needs more context per result, not just speed.

notable_replies.text: The accent-insensitive search is a lovely detail for multilingual notes.

I don't think speed was ever the main problem with search. The problem is that it looks like VS Code's search bar. When I'm trying to find something I wrote, I usually need more context around each result, and a sidebar is a poor fit for that.
whatever you did to make relevance work like it does. it made me want to buy you a kombucha.

text: Soon, your agents will be able to trace code back to the threads that produced it, giving them access to the decisions and reasoning the code alone can’t explain. https://t.co/zq5pXNvJxu
description: 12-second Zed teaser: a git-blame-style inline annotation in the editor links a line of Rust code back to the agent thread that produced it. A crisp reference for a micro-teaser that shows a single interaction in real product UI.
replies_summary: Developers like the idea ('git blame for agents') and joke about threads where someone said 'ship it anyway'. A few want it outside the GUI (an API, SDK or TUI), and some are wary of yet more agent tracking.
